---
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# CHEAT SHEET — everything below is a YAML comment. Quarto strips these
# before Pandoc ever sees them, so none of it reaches the published HTML.
#
# PUBLISH A CHANGE  (run from this folder, in the RStudio Terminal)
#   quarto render                 rebuild docs/  <- ALWAYS do this first,
#                                 GitHub Pages serves docs/, not the .qmd
#   git add .
#   git commit -m "message"
#   git push
#
# WORK ON IT LIVE
#   quarto preview                opens a browser, auto-reloads on save
#                                 Ctrl-C in the terminal to stop
#   quarto render index.qmd       rebuild one page instead of the whole site
#
# NEW BLOG POST
#   1. cp -r blog/posts/_template.qmd blog/posts/YYYY-MM-DD-slug/index.qmd
#      (make the folder first: mkdir blog/posts/YYYY-MM-DD-slug)
#   2. edit its title / description / date / categories
#   3. quarto render, then commit and push
#   The description field is what shows on the Writing page — write it.
#
# CHECK BEFORE YOU PANIC
#   git status                    what changed
#   git log --oneline -5          recent commits
#   git diff                      unstaged changes
#   git restore <file>            throw away edits to one file
#
# WHERE THINGS LIVE
#   theme.scss          all colours + type; $accent at the top drives the site
#   _quarto.yml         nav bar, footer, site-wide format options
#   files/              CV pdf and any other download — copied to docs/ on render
#   images/             portrait.jpg (resized); keep web images under ~200 KB
#   blog/posts/_metadata.yml   defaults every post inherits
#
# GOTCHAS
#   - Filenames are case-sensitive on GitHub Pages, not on your Mac.
#   - No spaces in filenames you link to.
#   - Pages takes 1-2 min to rebuild after a push; hard-refresh if unsure.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
pagetitle: "Yi Li"
listing:
  - id: recent
    contents: blog/posts
    type: default
    sort: "date desc"
    max-items: 3
    fields: [date, title, description]
    date-format: "MMM D, YYYY"
---

# Yi Li

::: {.hero-affil}
M.S. Applied Economics & Data Science · Expected 2027

I study macroeconomics, with a focus on macro-financial linkages and monetary policies. Before Penn, I studied economics and philosophy at Boston University.
This site is where I publish blog posts on interesting economic and data science analyses: what I pulled,
how I cleaned it, and what it actually shows and the economic content.
